govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HarrisLarryLSee:
Tom Belden wrote a viewpoint piece for the Dallas Morning News on November 22, 1977. His subject was the people who gather at Dealey Plaza. On the eve of the fourteenth anniversary of the assassination, doubters were assembling at the grassy knoll, the slope at the center of so many theories.

Anniversaries turned the plaza into a meeting place for the unconvinced. Belden, writing in the city's own paper, watched his hometown's wound become a yearly convention. The piece preserves how Dallas itself regarded the pilgrims who kept returning to the scene.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-VanderKerr_Van_: Chapter III of a book on the assassination looks at how Dallas television and radio covered the killing on Friday, November 22, 1963. Local stations were the first to carry the news, often with confused early reports. The chapter studies their broadcasts as both journalism and historical record. For media history, few days show live local coverage under pressure as clearly as that Friday in Dallas.
